A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear moments and the charge radii are in good agreement with predictions from shell model calculations.
the nuclear charge radii of the Sr isotopes are determined with an accuracy of 0.02–0.03 fm.
the charge radii of Sr nuclei are in general well reproduced by the relativistic mean field (RMF) calculations, but the magnetic and electric quadrupoles are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charge radii of the Sr nuclei are very sensitive to the deformation and that the anomalous coupling of the ground and isomeric states of 82,84Sr can be explained in terms of the shell model.
the charge radii and moments for 84–90Sr are well described by the Skyrme Hartree-Fock model, while the lighter nuclei 82,83Sr are not.
the nuclear deformation in light Sr nuclei is not a simple function of the number of valence neutrons, and the anomalous behavior is not restricted to the ground state.
